title: Fix athena land --pr base branch and work-branch contents
summary: The PR base becomes the remote's default branch as GitHub reports it (a REST read of the repository), not the local current branch. The pushed athena/<job> branch becomes a commit that carries the candidate plus the job's records (verification, outcome, etc.), so merging it lands what `athena check --history` expects. Both get tests; merge stays behind `merge_via_rest`.

defaults_applied.how: Add unit tests for both fixes; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change in gh.rs and its caller, with a git helper only if needed.
Behavior criteria are checked with cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Recovered the records-on-local-HEAD layout and fake-based test pattern from the repository.

assumptions: Records are committed on the user's local branch (HEAD), so the work branch should be the candidate combined with the records from local HEAD (e.g. a merge or records-tree commit on top of the candidate); the exact construction is the producer's choice if the fingerprint stays equal to the verified one.
The default branch is read from `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` field `default_branch`.
Pushed head/link.head and the checks lookup should use the new pushed commit rather than the bare candidate.

acceptance_criteria.text: PrHost (or GhClient) gains a call that reads the repository's default branch via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` (`default_branch` field); Athena::land_pr uses it as NewPr.base and no longer uses git current_branch for the base.
A detached HEAD or a local branch absent from the remote no longer affects the PR base or errors.

The commit pushed to athena/<job> contains the candidate's content plus the job's records (verification, outcome, candidate and other records) from the local history, and is a descendant of the verified candidate so the push guard and fingerprint check still hold.
The merge call remains reachable only when `merge_via_rest` is true and checks are green; that gate and its default (off) are unchanged.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`: a new test using fake Runner/PrHost shows the base is the host-reported default branch (e.g. `trunk`) while the local branch differs; a new test shows the pushed commit includes the records files, not just the candidate commit.
Run `cargo test` , `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass; existing land_pr tests still pass.

out_of_scope: Enabling merge by default or changing the merge_via_rest setting
Force pushes or other branches than athena/<job>
departures: The second bug needs real git plumbing (building a commit with records) and tests against a git repo, so cost and time are above the reference.
